newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity trades lower in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity trades lower in thin volume.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures eased Wednesday in thin volume with some weakness from weather forecasts and speculation on the effects of planned changes to transmission on the Pacific Intertie, sources said.

As of 1210 EDT, September Palo Verde (PV) electricity was down 67 cents at $29.10 per megawatt hour (MWh) after exchanges in a range of $28.85-29.60, while October was 60 cents lower at $22.50 per MWh.
September California Oregon Border (COB) was down 23 cents at $22.25 following exchanges in a range of $22.10-22.60, while October was 20 cents lower at $21.50 per MWh.
NYMEX said that as of 1130 EDT an estimated total of 284 PV and 52 COB contracts had traded.
"The weather is pretty stable right now, but what we also may be seeing is some speculation plays on the intertie," said a New York futures trader.

Capacity on the Pacific Intertie transmission system, the main conduit moving cheap Northwest hydropower to southern California, should be raised by 600 megawatts (MW) to 6,900 MW no later than 2400 PDT Monday.

The Intertie's current 6,300 MW rating will expire Thursday, but the limit would likely be extended if the new 6,900 MW rating is not implemented by then, the Western Systems Coordinating Council said.
Separately, discharge from the 6,150 MW Grand Coulee hydropower dam, the uppermost U.S. project on the Columbia River, were being slowed, meaning less power generation through Monday.

Three western power units -- a 260 MW Hayden coal-fired unit in Colorado, a 550 MW Jim Bridger coal-fired unit in Wyoming, and a 600 MW Grand Coulee hydroturbine in Washington -- were set to resume operations today after unplanned repairs.
The 254 MW unit 1 at the Valmy coal-fired power plant in Nevada will likely be off line for a week after being shut Monday due to a rotor problem.
The 750 MW Four Corners coal-fired unit 5 in New Mexico, shut earlier this month to repair a high pressure generator field, was planned to restart next week.
The 1,221 MW Palo Verde 2 nuclear power unit in Arizona began slowly coasting down to its September refueling outage.

The latest six- to 10-day forecasts showed the West would experience seasonal to slightly cooler-than-seasonal readings regionwide with a monsoonal flow bringing above-normal precipitation in the mountainous areas.
COB open interest for July 29 fell 72 to 5,528 while PV open interest declined 32 to 5,520, NYMEX said.
